data.why: The app ships its own built-in Sun-to-Pluto body catalogue (no uploads); manim_viz.py is replaced with a stub because manim's manimpango dependency needs system cairo/pango headers that cannot be installed here, and app.py unconditionally imports manim_viz at module load time.

goals: Pick a two-body system (e.g. Earth-Moon) and derive the mass ratio mu and orbital period
Compute all five Lagrange points and classify each as stable or unstable via linearised eigenvalue analysis
Perturb a satellite placed at a Lagrange point (radial, tangential, or velocity nudge) and integrate its trajectory with REBOUND's IAS15 integrator
Inspect the trajectory in the rotating frame (2D plane and 3D effective-potential terrain) and read off telemetry: max deviation, Jacobi constant, mu, orbital period
Compare libration versus escape behavior by repeating the perturbation experiment across L1-L5

review.summary: The tree follows the README's experiment closely, and the six screens I opened all show what their nodes claim, so the structure is sound. It still needs fixes before filing: it mislabels the position trims, repeats the app's wrong 'AU' unit and its partly hard-coded stability verdict, and misses or mis-tests map placement and video export.
